With careful planning and temporary heat provision plans by contractor this could also permit work during heating season. We anticipate evaluating proposals with at least 1 factor demonstrating a contractor s utilization of these updates to indicate their time and cost savings relative to off-hours work. This presents an excellent opportunity for the awardee to utilize the winter of 26/27 to procure materials, complete admin and detailed coordination drawings for building 1, while utilizing immediately available work in buildings 15 and 16 to establish team dynamics, rhythm, and process to build steam. Are there any specific needs of the facility? Can a contractor utilize temporary heaters? Can a contractor bring in an engineering team to help assist? Rough sizing calcs demonstrating heating loads are satisfied Advantages: Copper/pluming work vs schedule 80 pipe welding. Elimination of smaller condensate pumps such as PTOT, customer care suite, canteen, mech room (still one in sub-basement), elimination of canteen CP by Walk-in. VA Response: VA will take a look at the requirements, but having a qualified MEP Coordinator on this specific job is the intention. Is there the ability for an administrative NTP to be issued? PROJECT DESCRIPTION The scope of this project is to replace all data infrastructure across the Gainesville VAMC and to build a new data center to support that upgraded system. The data center building will be one story, and the footprint will be approximately 3,931 SF at the location of temporary trailer 11, which will be demolished as part of this project. The primary space within the building is the 1,177 SF Data Center Room. Supporting spaces include Unpacking/Packing/Staging, Entrance Room, and Storage. Mechanical, Electrical, and HVAC spaces. Additionally, a new generator will be housed in a separate Generator Room. Also, this project will be removing all existing equipment and cabling affiliated with the telecom rooms in all campus buildings. There are 59 telecom rooms that may require architectural work. Some rooms are existing TRs being reused, but most are new rooms being redesigned for the telecom equipment. In rare cases telecom enclosures are recommended and/or exceptions will be required. The entire campus will be occupied while work occurs. Contractor will have to coordinate room closures and shutdowns with the COR. Most rooms on campus will be affected. Some off-hour work is anticipated for more critical spaces. ADMINISTRATIVE The solicitation will be issued as an Invitation for Bids (IFB) conducted in accordance with FAR part 14 and will be evaluated in accordance with the procedures listed in the solicitation. The solicitation will be issued as a total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside. Offers received from other than SDVOSB concerns will not be considered. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220 with a size standard of $45.0 million. The solicitation will be issued in mid to late July 2026, with an estimated late September 2026 award. The period of performance is approximately 921 calendar days from the issuance of the notice to proceed. In accordance with VAAR 836.204, the magnitude of construction is between $20,000,000 and $50,000,000 (although the middle of this range is more relevant). title: This effort encompasses all technical, logistical, software and hardware efforts required to produce CCS Meadowlands systems.
description: Purpose: This is a Sources Sought. The Space Systems Command (SSC) located at Los Angeles Air Force Base, California, is seeking information in the form of Statements of Capabilities (SOC) from interested parties in support of the SSC, Space Domain Awareness and Combat Power Directorate requirement for the Counter Communications System (CCS) Meadowlands as described below. The Government is conducting market research to inform its Acquisition Strategy. The purpose of this notice is to identify potential sources that can meet CFC/MD3�s requirement. The Government reserves the right to set this acquisition, or portions thereof, aside for small business � to include socially and economically disadvantaged businesses, 8(a) firms, or woman-owned businesses. The Government is seeking contractors interested in and capable of providing all technical and logistical effort required to design, develop, and deliver capabilities to support the CCS Meadowlands system. Background and Description: Scope: This effort encompasses all technical, logistical, software and hardware efforts required to produce CCS Meadowlands systems. Period and Place of Performance: It is envisioned that the period of performance will be approximately 12 months in duration. The Government is working through the details to determine when the contract will start. The place of performance is flexible to allow contractor to provide an optimized solution. Background: CCS System: CCS is a ground-based counter satellite communications (SATCOM) system specifically designed to reversibly deny, disrupt, and degrade adversarial SATCOM. The basic CCS concept is to provide a flexible, modular, scalable, rapidly deployable system with a key set of signal processing/generation (SP) capabilities, selected counter SATCOM missions, and a robust transmit capability. Its architecture will be designed to host core capabilities and/or other more sophisticated �plug and play� type modules to address the ever-increasing number of technologies and assets available to our adversaries. The latest CCS Meadowlands will have upgraded capabilities compared to the existing CCS 10.2 Systems. The future CCS Meadowlands fleet will be composed of at least 32 systems. Meadowlands is a transportable SATCOM system composed of modular Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) / Government Off-The-Shelf (GOTS) Radio Frequency (RF) monitoring and generation equipment. The design incorporates multi-band antennas and equipment in transit cases. The frequency conversion system (FCS) that handles RF signals between the shelter transit cases to the antenna uses a proprietary photonics system. The system can be transported by C-130 or larger aircraft and by ground transport over improved or semi-improved roads. The system will be designed for operations by trained operators in US-controlled facilities world-wide, and in the Developmental Support Facility (DSF). The Meadowlands �Base Design� system meets current A-spec requirements. All systems have same Transit Case and Antenna configuration/capability. The Meadowlands base design system is comprised of the following major capabilities: Three independent, bidirectional antenna polarization paths Native Support for a single Large Multiband Antenna (LMA) Bands Supported: UHF, L, C, Ku, Ka Two separate independently controlled antenna polarization paths Simultaneous dual polarization operation Receive-only operation if desired Supports Base, and unique network specific missions Native Support for a single 1.2m Antenna Antenna Supports L-Band only The system can operate in three antenna Polarization Paths � Each Polarization Path Contains an Uplink & Downlink RF Interface. The system is capable of simultaneously operating/controlling up to three antennas and associated components utilizing three polarization paths. The Meadowlands system utilizes Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) Ethernet, TCP & UDP/IP Standard interfaces for network communications (Data, Command, Control & Status) between Transit case assemblies, Antennas and the Software Server The Base System Configuration is composed of: 4 System Transit Cases in Shelter (Mission Control & Timing (MCT) Subsystem, Advanced Signal Processor (ASP) Subsystem, Shelter Photonics Unit (SPU1), SPU2) 1 Antenna Transit Case in Shelter for 1.2m Antenna (1.2m Transit Case) 1 Transit Case for Secure External Network Operations (Remote Ops Transit Case) � Contains Firewall & Encryption 2 Transit Cases outside by LMA antenna (Antenna Photonics Unit (APU)2 & APU2) APU Transit Cases The system can operate in the UHF, L, C, Ku, and KA RF Bands for Transmit and Receive via Frequency Conversion System (FCS) The production of the CCS Meadowlands units has been accomplished as part of a Pre-Planned Product Improvement effort. description: Introduction/Background The U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Armaments Center (DEVCOM AC) Munitions Engineering Technology Center (METC), Medium and Cannon Caliber Munitions Division FCDD-ACM-MJ at Picatinny Arsenal, NJ is issuing this sources sought notice to conduct market research to determine the ability to perform complete life cycle engineering for a wide variety of munition systems across DEVCOM AC for various customers. This includes exploratory, advanced and engineering development, experimental testing, quality engineering, evaluation and qualification of munition systems and component concepts, as well as production and manufacturing engineering for munition systems and components. 2.Disclaimer THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A �REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP)� TO BE SUBMITTED. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. RESPONSES WILL NOT BE RETURNED TO THE RESPONDER. NOT RESPONDING TO THIS NOTICE DOES NOT PRECLUDE PARTICIPATION IN ANY FUTURE REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) OR INVITATION FOR BID (IFB) OR RFP, IF ANY ISSUED. IT IS THE RESPONSIBILITY OF POTENTIAL OFFERORS TO MONITOR THE GPE FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION PERTAINING TO THIS REQUIREMENT. 3.Requirements: 3.1 The Contractor shall provide qualified engineering professionals to perform comprehensive engineering functions supporting the research, design, development, test and evaluation, production, and sustainment of advanced munition systems. The Contractor shall apply engineering competencies to solve complex technical challenges throughout the munition system lifecycle by executing rigorous engineering activities. The Contractor shall apply core engineering disciplines by executing critical technical activities such as performing requirements decomposition and system architecture design; creating detailed Computer-Aided Design (CAD) models; conducting structural, thermal, and kinematic finite element analysis (FEA); designing analog and digital circuit boards; developing embedded software and control algorithms; and formulating developmental test plans alongside post-test data reduction. Through these tasks, the Contractor shall deliver engineering artifacts such as Interface Control Documents (ICDs), Technical Data Packages (TDPs), simulation reports, and software version descriptions and actively participate in formal/informal reviews to ensure robust engineering rigor, standard methodologies, and scientific discipline are applied to the development, production, and sustainment of the munition systems. They will review designs and Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs) against military and commercial specifications, Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) standards, and producibility standards and proactively identifying opportunities to reduce costs, accelerate schedules, optimize manufacturing processes, and elevate overall quality. Throughout the life cycle, the contractor shall be responsible for supporting project preparation encompassing planning, cost analysis, scheduling, facility coordination, and integration. Finally, they shall be responsible for collaborating with multi-disciplinary program teams to support the reliable delivery and sustained performance of munition systems, aligning all efforts with operational utility and organizational mission requirements. 3.2 The individuals are expected to travel on a semi-regular basis. 3.3 The Contractor shall attend, support, and report on meetings, review documents, contribute to the preparation of original documents, analyze cost, performance, risk, and provide recommendations or courses of action and ensure objectives are met. 3.4 The Contractor shall support the generation and review of briefing materials. 3.5 The Contractor shall support, coordinate, participate, and record regular Integrated Product Team (IPT) meetings on assigned projects/programs. 3.6 The Contractor shall provide technical advice regarding project feasibility, definitions of project scope, complexities/risk involved, phases required, and time schedules. 3.7 The Contractor shall keep project team leads/ Armaments Project Officer (APO) and Branch and Division supervisors informed of program/project status, issues, problems and recommendations through oral communication, proper documentation including trip reports and attendance at regularly scheduled and informal meetings. Provide technical support and advice to project team leads/APOs and Branch and Division supervisors on engineering aspects of assigned munition systems. This shall include solution recommendations regarding major problems and conflicting requirements with assigned projects/programs. 4. Background The applicable NAICS code for this requirement is 541330 Engineering Services and the PSC code is R425 Engineering and Technical Services. Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capability statement. 5. Submission Details Interested contractors are strongly encouraged to submit a capabilities statement with the following information: 5.1 Ability to provide a product that meets the above specifications. 5.2 Historical information demonstrating that you have the ability to provide the product (contract number(s), dollar value(s), Point of Contacts, and brief description of work performed). 5.3 In addition, please provide full company name and address, point of contact with telephone number and email address, CAGE Code and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number, size of business (i.e. large, small, disadvantaged, veteran owned, woman owned, etc.) and applicable NAICS, Product Service Code (PSC), and website (if applicable). All data should be provided at no cost to the US Government by October 3, 2026 at 3PM EDT. 5.4 Contractors must be properly registered in the Government System for Award Management database (SAM). Contractors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation of requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220, or via the Internet at www.sam.gov. 5.5 This is a market survey for information only and shall not be construed as a request for a proposal or as an obligation on the part of the US Government. The US Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this market survey or otherwise pay for information solicited. 5.6 The official response must be submitted to: The US Army Contracting Command - Rock Island at Picatinny, ATTN: Contracting/Agreements Officer: Charlotte Sylvain-Ceraul, charlotte.a.sylvain-ceraul.civ@army.mil and Contract Specialist: Qendresa Neza, qendresa.neza.civ@army.mil. description: This sole-source justification provides authority to award a task order on the basis of other than full and open competition for Systems Engineering and Technical Assistance (SETA) support services. The contractor will perform SETA services to assist the SC Security Technology Integration Program (STIP) in system development and operations and maintenance (O&M). This includes providing technical guidance throughout the acquisition lifecycle and systems engineering life cycle (SELC), reviewing open architecture (OA), System of Systems (SoS), design documentation, and supporting risk management activities. The contractor will also assist in developing and maintaining documentation, reviewing operational processes for compliance and efficiency, supporting incident response and troubleshooting, and execution of major initiatives within STIP and related security technology efforts. These services will ensure accurate reporting and device connectivity to TSANetwork (TSANet) via the Security Technology Information eXchange (STIX) for alarm counts and throughput data. The contractor will validate the accuracy and integrity of system-generated reports, support improvements to reporting tools, and ensure compliance with Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and TSA data standards. Additionally, the contractor will review and validate device integration with TSANet, verify data transmission protocols, and assist in resolving connectivity issues to ensure reliable data collection and aggregation. STIP is the interface of Secure Flight (SF), Credential Authentication Technology CAT 2 (CAT-2), enhanced metal detectors (EMDs), and connectivity of other Transportation Security Equipment (TSE). These TSEs enhance the capabilities necessary to sustain TSA�s mission-critical operations, equip the frontline, and safeguard the traveling public. STIP provides the connection between TSEs located in airports and the TSANet for sharing of mission, and operational and maintenance data. Specifically, STIP enables network connectivity for exchanging the near-real time passenger vetting status of more than 1.7 million passengers daily between TSA�s SF system and over 2,100 CAT / CAT-2 units deployed at airports across the country. Without a STIP connection, that data cannot be shared with the checkpoints and data is performed manually by Transportation Security Officers (TSOs) on an hourly basis. SETA support services are paramount to providing technical monitoring of the STIP platform including analysis of vulnerabilities to the system and identification of process improvements and efficiencies to current and continuous operational changes. Only B&B can provide the required continuity of services with the highest level of confidence while maintaining support for active and time-sensitive SC initiatives and operations and maintenance services. These SC initiatives include ensuring successful management and completion of Advanced Imaging Technology (AIT) connectivity, Security Technology Information eXchange (STIX) connectivity, and operational utility evaluation (OUE) activities by November 2026; ensuring successful management and completion of the STIP database server migration to Windows Server 19 by January 2027; ensuring successful completion and operational readiness of the Data Center 15 (DC15) development lab by March 2027; and ensuring successful management and completion of ongoing STIP engineering change requests (ECRs), enhancements, and O&M. +++++++++++++

title: Diffuusiokapasiteetti/Spirometrialaitteistot
description: Diffuusiokapasiteetti/Spirometrialaitteistot Hankinnan kohteena on Etelä-Savon hyvinvointialueen (Eloisa) Mikkelin keskussairaalaan tuleva diffuusiokapasiteetti-/spirometrialaitteisto (1 kpl) sekä laitekohtaiset kulutustarvikkeet, ohjelmisto, lisenssit ja huoltopalvelu. Hankinnassa on lisäksi optio kahdelle (2) vastaavanlaiselle laitekokonaisuudelle (diffuusiokapasiteetti-/spirometrialaitteistot) sekä yhdelle (1) spirometrialaitteistolle. Eloisa päättää mahdollisten optioiden hankkimisesta vuoden 2028 loppuun mennessä. Sopimuskausi alkaa sopimuksen allekirjoittamisesta. Sopimus allekirjoitetaan mahdollisimman pian lainvoimaisen päätöksen jälkeen. Sopimus on toistaiseksi voimassa oleva. Laitteen tulee soveltua diffuusiokapasiteetin mittaamiseen ja spirometriatutkimusten tekemiseen. Spirometria ja diffuusiokapasiteetti ovat keskeisiä keuhkojen toimintakokeita. Spirometrialla mitataan keuhkojen tilavuutta ja ilman virtausta, mikä auttaa tunnistamaan ahtauttavat (esim. astma, COPD) tai rajoittavat keuhkosairaudet. Diffuusiokapasiteetti mittaa kaasujen siirtymistä keuhkorakkuloista vereen, ja sitä käytetään keuhkokudoksen sairauksien (esim. fibroosi) arvioinnissa. Laitteella tulee pystyä tekemään spirometria ja bronkodilataatiokoe, diffuusiokoe hengityslihasvoiman mittaus sekä SNIP. Pyydettäessä tarjoaja toimittaa kustannuksellaan tarjotun laitteistokokonaisuuden koekäyttöön Mikkelin keskussairaalalle. Tarjouspyyntö julkaistaan ehdollisena optioiden osalta: optioiden hankinnat voidaan toteuttaa, mikäli hankinnoille varatut investointimäärärahat hyväksytään.,

description: 1. Purpose The Department of War (DoW) is conducting market research to identify interested and capable businesses that can provide test pilot training in support of the US Air Force Security Assistance Training (AFSAT) squadron. This Sources Sought Notice is issued for market research and planning purposes only. Responses will be used to assess market capability, commercial availability, acquisition alternatives, and the availability of small-business concerns capable of performing the anticipated requirement as a prime contractor. 2. Anticipated Mandatory Institutional Accreditations, Approvals, and Credentials The Government anticipates that a future solicitation may require the successful contractor to maintain the following institutional accreditations, approvals, and credentials. Respondents shall provide verifiable documentation of their current status, including the issuing organization, approval/accreditation number where applicable, scope, effective date, expiration date, and any pending renewal or limitation. description: Η δημοπρατούμενη σύμβαση, για λόγους επίτευξης καλύτερου λειτουργικού αποτελέσματος, είναι και δημοπρατείται ως σύμβαση «με το κλειδί στο χέρι» (turn-key project), υπό την έννοια ότι ο Ανάδοχος αναλαμβάνει στο πλαίσιο των αναλυτικών προδιαγραφών και λειτουργικών απαιτήσεων της παρούσας να παραδώσει κάθε έναν από τους δώδεκα (12) συρμούς έξι (6) οχημάτων της σειράς Ι, δηλαδή συνολικά εβδομήντα δύο (72) οχήματα, πλήρως αναβαθμισμένα, με διάρκεια ζωής (service life) 25 χρόνια από την ολοκλήρωση της σύμβασης. Συνοπτικά το αντικείμενο περιλαμβάνει σύμφωνα με τους όρους του συνόλου των συμβατικών τευχών: Α1) Την εκπόνηση της Μελέτης. Α2) Την αναβάθμιση, δοκιμή και θέση σε λειτουργία δώδεκα (12) συρμών, των έξι (6) οχημάτων εκάστου με ονομαστική τάση λειτουργίας 750Vdc. Α3) Την προμήθεια των ειδικών εργαλείων, του διαγνωστικού εξοπλισμού δοκιμών και ομοιώματος, όπως αυτά ορίζονται στη Σύμβαση. Α4) Την τριετή εγγύηση καλής λειτουργίας των συρμών και την προμήθεια των ανταλλακτικών και αναλώσιμων ανταλλακτικών της περιόδου θέσης σε λειτουργία, καθώς και των ανταλλακτικών και αναλώσιμων ανταλλακτικών της περιόδου εγγύησης που απαιτούνται για τις περιόδους αυτές. Α5) Την σύνταξη και υποβολή των τευχών τεκμηρίωσης, των εγχειριδίων συντήρησης και λειτουργίας και των εικονογραφημένων καταλόγων ανταλλακτικών. Α6) Την εκπαίδευση του προσωπικού της ΣΤΑΣΥ. B) Την προμήθεια των ανταλλακτικών αρχικής υποστήριξης, όπως αναλυτικά περιλαμβάνονται στο συνημμένο στο έντυπο οικονομικής προσφοράς «Πίνακας Ανταλλακτικών Αρχικής Υποστήριξης». Οι ως άνω απαιτούμενες προμήθειες και υπηρεσίες, καθώς και οι αναλυτικές τους τεχνικές προδιαγραφές περιγράφονται στο τεύχος των Τεχνικών Προδιαγραφών (εφεξής ΤΠ). Τα προς προμήθεια είδη κατατάσσονται στους ακόλουθους κωδικούς του Κοινού Λεξιλογίου για τις Δημόσιες Συμβάσεις (CPV) : • 34622100-4 Επιβατικά βαγόνια αστικού σιδηροδρόμου. • 34630000-2 Μέρη σιδηροδρομικών ή τροχιοδρομικών μηχανών έλξης ή τροχαίου υλικού· εξοπλισμός ελέγχου της κυκλοφορίας για σιδηροδρόμους. • 50222000-7 Υπηρεσίες επισκευής και συντήρησης τροχαίου εξοπλισμού. Η εκτιμώμενη αξία της σύμβασης ανέρχεται στο ποσό των εκατόν εννέα εκατομμυρίων ευρώ (109.000.000 €) μη συμπεριλαμβανομένου ΦΠΑ. Ο προϋπολογισμός αναλύεται ως εξής: Α) Για τα ανωτέρω υπ’ αρίθμ. Α1 έως Α6, ποσό εκατόν έξι εκατομμύρια πεντακόσιες χιλιάδες Ευρώ (106.500.000€) χωρίς ΦΠΑ. Β) Για τα ανωτέρω υπ’ αρίθμ. Β, ποσό δύο εκατομμυρίων και πεντακοσίων χιλιάδων Ευρώ (2.500.000) χωρίς ΦΠΑ Επισημαίνεται ότι οι οικονομικές προσφορές που θα δοθούν δεν θα υπερβαίνουν το συνολικό προϋπολογισμό, αλλά ούτε και τους επιμέρους προϋπολογισμούς των ανωτέρω πεδίων (Α) και (Β).

description: Project Title: Design-Build Repair and Renovation of the Gulf Marine Service Facility (GMSF) & Wharf Repairs, in Pascagoula, Mississippi Location: 151 Watts Ave, Pascagoula, MS 39567 Classification and General Information: This requirement will be issued as a Total Small Business Set-Aside. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code associated with this procurement is 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The Small Business Administration standard of $45.0 million dollars in annual receipts averaged over a business�s latest three (3) complete fiscal years or (except in the Business Loan, Disaster Loan Programs, Surety Bond Guarantee, and SBIC Programs) five (5) complete fiscal years to determine the average annual receipts. If a business hasn�t been in business for five (5) years, multiply its average weekly revenue by 52 to determine its average annual receipts. This requirement will be a Total Small Business Set-Aside, and the contractor shall be selected using Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) Part 36.101-2 Use of Two-Phase Design-Build Selection Procedures and RFO Part 15.1 Presolicitation and Solicitation procedures. This procurement will be competitive, utilizing the Highest-Technically Rated with a Fair and Reasonable Process approach based on the solicitations�s stated budgetary constraints (affordability) under the Best Value (RFO Part 15.103). The approach prioritizes the best possible performance, provided the price is determined to be fair and reasonable and within the guidelines of the Government�s stated budget. During each phase, all proposals are initially evaluated based solely on the non-price factors specified in the solicitation. Only the price of the highest-ranked technical proposal is then evaluated to ensure it is fair, reasonable and does not exceed our stated budget. All evaluation factors other than cost or price, when combined, are significantly more important than cost or price. This requirement will result in a Firm-Fixed-Price contract for design and construction services. Background Overview: The GMSF is a critical NOAA asset located in Pascagoula, Mississippi, and is a shared-use site for both the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) and the Office of Marine and Aviation Operations (OMAO). The facility consists of a berthing wharf and pier, seawall, and upland warehouse buildings essential for supporting NOAA's mission in the Gulf of America Region. See Figure 1 for the GMSF site plan (See Attachment). The facility has sustained damage from recent hurricane and storm events, primarily affecting the wharf structure. Additionally, the steel sheet pile wall has sustained damage from exposure to the Pascagoula River, resulting in section loss of the sheets and subsequent loss of fill material behind the seawall. This loss of material has resulted in sink holes in the wharf operational area. The existing wharf and pier is approximately 540 feet long and 26 feet wide, and was constructed in three sections (referred to as the North, Middle and South sections). The wharf structure is integral with a steel sheet pile seawall. Each wharf section has been repaired in some form over the past several decades, primarily to address the failing seawall. A portion of the wharf overhangs the Pascagoula River. See Figure 2 for a typical section through the wharf (See Attachment). As-built drawings for each section of wharf are available and will be provided with the formally issued solicitation documents. NOAA�s ships homeported at GMSF are operated by two separate line offices - NMFS and OMAO. Mooring configurations at GMSF vary based on the operations of each line office. Refer to Table 1 (See Attachment) for information regarding the size of the NOAA ships homeported at GMSF, and to Figure 3 (See Attachment) for example mooring arrangements. Project Description - Generally described as follows but not limited to: This project is a direct response to the damages sustained from storm events and exposure to corrosive environments, and is intended to restore the facility to its full operational capacity. The project's primary focus will be the evaluation and repair of the wharf, seawall, mooring structures, and utilities. In addition to repairs, this project will include upgrades to the wharf�s structural and electrical infrastructure, with a specific focus on hardening against future storm events. The project will also require an assessment of the operational efficiency of the wharf working area, and potential relocation of components (i.e. light poles, etc) to improve efficiency and safety. Key elements expected to be addressed include, but are not limited to: Restore the integrity of the deteriorating seawall and mooring structures. Evaluate and renovate the existing wharf sections to allow for NOAA ships to be moored securely during hurricane conditions. Potential addition of in-water mooring structures or dolphins. Corrosion protection of the wharf and pier to protect from long-term corrosive environments. Upgrades of necessary utility infrastructure for ship connections, with specific attention to electrical deficiencies. Assessment of operational areas of the wharf and making revisions to correct any safety and efficiency issues. Site utility upgrades, to include addition of emergency generator ports for the upland warehouses and routing of power to existing parking lot. Unique Challenges Heavy Weather Mooring The project must accommodate a critical NOAA operational constraint: NOAA vessels remain moored during severe wind (hurricane) and wave events. The contractor shall ensure the wharf design capacity fully supports the maximum mooring line loads anticipated during these storm events. NOAA will provide a coastal and mooring analysis with the formally issued solicitation to provide initial definition of the ship loading on the wharf. The DB contractor should anticipate the need to validate this analysis and further refine it during the design phase. South Mooring Bollard NOAA utilizes a mooring bollard at the south end of GMSF that sits upon a seawall that is not maintained by NOAA. The seawall, which is owned and maintained by the City of Pascagoula, appears to be failing beneath the mooring bollard. It should be anticipated that close coordination with the City will be required to address this bollard. Refer to Figure 1 (See Attachment) for location of the South Mooring Bollard, and to Figure 4 (See Attachment) showing the current condition of the bollard and seawall. On this item in particular, NOAA is looking for innovative solutions from the DB team. Potential solutions include, but are not limited to, repair or reinforcement of the existing seawall to continue supporting this bollard, or relocating the bollard to a new in-water mooring structure. Site Visit Information: There is no site visit planned as part of Phase I. Offerors will have the opportunity to visit the site before submission of their technical and price proposals as part of Phase II. The site visit details, to be held at the GMSF & Wharf, will be outlined in the Phase II solicitation package. Currently the site visit is projected to be held on or about January 12, 2027. If applicable, all required site access information as outlined in Section J of the Phase II RFP must be submitted in accordance with the solicitation requirements for site visit entry. description: Le présent accord-cadre a pour objet de définir les termes contractuels généraux : Entre le pouvoir adjudicateur et l’opérateur économique [titulaire de l’AC] Dans le cadre de la passation de futurs Marchés Subséquents (MS) relatifs aux prestations de matériels audiovisuels de diffusion avec ou sans installation couvertes par le présent accord-cadre. Ainsi, les prestations sont décrites de manière générale dans les cahiers des charges de l’accord-cadre (CCAP, CCTP et annexes) et seront décrites avec précision dans le cahier des clauses particulières valant acte d’engagement (CCP valant AE) et annexes de chaque futur marché subséquent qui sera contractualisé avec le titulaire de l’accord cadre retenu après demande du pouvoir adjudicateur à celui-ci de compléter son offre conformément à la partie II du CCAP. NB : la passation des marchés subséquents (MS) est réalisée dans les conditions mentionnées au titre II du présent document. Forme de l'accord - cadre : Il s’agit d’un accord-cadre mono-attributaire donnant ensuite lieu à la conclusion de marchés subséquents. Le présent accord-cadre a pour objet de définir les termes contractuels généraux entre le pouvoir adjudicateur et l’opérateur économique (titulaire de l’AC), dans le cadre de la passation de futurs Marchés Subséquents (MS) relatifs aux prestations de fourniture avec ou sans installation de matériels audiovisuels par le présent accord-cadre. Ainsi, les prestations sont décrites de manière générale dans les cahiers des charges de l’accord-cadre (CCAP, CCTP et annexes) et seront décrites avec précision dans le cahier des clauses particulières valant acte d’engagement (CCP valant AE) et annexes de chaque futur marché subséquent qui sera contractualisé avec le titulaire de l’accord cadre. Motif de non allotissement : -La dévolution en lots séparés est de nature à restreindre la concurrence en effet le secteur de l’audiovisuel est structuré autour d'opérateurs dits « intégrateurs ». Le fractionnement du marché en deux lots (fourniture d'une part, fourniture et installation d'autre part) serait uniquement artificiel. Il existe une absence d'opérateurs spécialisés sur le seul segment de fourniture. En effet, les grossistes (vente pure) ne répondent pas ou peu aux marchés publics incluant ou non du service. Par ailleurs, la dévolution en lots séparés risque de rendre techniquement difficile ou financièrement plus coûteuse l'exécution des prestations en effet la séparation des prestations engendrerait un surcoût mécanique. C’est un vrai levier de massification, car le matériel représentant la part prépondérante du budget, le lot unique permet de négocier des tarifs « grands comptes » auprès des constructeurs. Allotir reviendrait à diviser les volumes et donc à subir des prix unitaires (BPU) plus élevés pour des matériels identiques ; Description technique : les prestations sont définies dans le Cahier des Clauses Techniques Particulières (CCTP) et ses annexes. Accord-cadre mono attributaire : pour l’accord cadre, il sera retenu 1 titulaire Les offres sont valables 4 mois à compter de la date limite fixée pour la réception des plis. title: Czechia – Architectural and related services – Městský dům na náměstí Republiky v Tachově
description: Předmětem soutěže je návrh novostavby polyfunkčního městského domu na náměstí Republiky v Tachově. Nový objekt nahradí stávající Dům potravin, jehož technický stav, dispoziční řešení a architektonická kvalita již nevyhovují současným požadavkům a bude demolován. Cílem soutěže je nalézt kvalitní, soudobý, realistický architektonický návrh, který bude mít společenský a kulturní přínos, dodá nové impulzy do centra města, posílí jeho atraktivitu, přispěje ke kultivaci prostoru a přirozeně naváže na charakter historického prostředí městské památkové zóny. Návrh by měl přirozeně doplnit městskou strukturu historického jádra a kultivovaně navázat na charakter místa. Dům by měl být sebevědomý a zároveň pokorný, vyjadřovat svým jazykem současnost, ale zároveň respekt k městské památkové zóně, do níž vstupuje, a vytvořit přirozenou součást kulturní paměťové vrstvy Tachova. Vybranému účastníkovi vzešlému ze soutěže o návrh bude následně zadána kompletní zakázka na zpracování všech fází projektové dokumentace a nezbytných souvisejících služeb, které jsou podmínkou úspěšné realizace a provozování městského domu, a to při optimalizaci nákladů a kvality stavby s ohledem na její celoživotní cyklus. Zadavatel předpokládá realizaci zakázky bezprostředně po ukončení soutěže o návrh.

title: Belgium – Construction work – RESTAURATIE EN HERBESTEMMING VAN HET HEILIGE GEESTHUIS IN LIER
description: Het Godshuis Heilig Geesthuis bestaat uit vier gebouwen geschikt rond een binnenplaats. In het dossier worden de gebouwen als volgt benoemd; voorbouw gebouw A, westvleugel gebouw B, achterbouw gebouw C en oostvleugel gebouw D. Na een doorgedreven restauratie zal het gebouwensemble worden herbestemd als ‘Huis van het Kind’. De gebouwen worden aangepast aan de technische en comfort eisen van het Huis van het Kind met aandacht voor energie, duurzaamheid, toegankelijkheid , kindveiligheid en brand. De gebouwschil van gebouw A en C worden grondig gerenoveerd (herstel gevelparament, vernieuwen of restaureren buitenschijnwerk en vernieuwen van de dakbedekking). De houten draagstructuren, zowel verdiepingsvloeren als dakkap, worden in beide gebouwen doorgedreven hersteld of vernieuwd. Het interieur wordt aangepast aan de hedendaagse comforteisen met totale vernieuwing van alle technieken en het implementeren van een lift en nieuwe trapkern. Waar mogelijk wordt langs binnen geïsoleerd. Gebouw C wordt bijkomend volledig onderkelderd. Gebouw B wordt afgebroken en vervangen door een nieuwbouwvolume van één bouwlaag met een gradueel vertrapte dakspeelplaats die de verbinding tussen gebouwdelen A en C maakt op de verdiepingen. Ook de nieuwbouw B wordt voorzien van een nieuwe ondergrondse kelder. De binnenplaats, die wordt vergroot door de afbraak van gebouw D, wordt volledig heraangelegd. De eertijds gedempte Sint-Pietersvliet achter achterbouw C wordt terug opengewerkt en publiek ontsloten. Het project beoogt een duurzame verwarming van het Heilige Geestgebouw via een combinatie van aquathermie (warmte uit oppervlaktewater) en geothermie (BEO-veld). De toepassing van aquathermie kadert binnen een Europees Interreg-subsidieproject, waarbij het Heilige Geestgebouw fungeert als pilootproject voor duurzame energie in erfgoedcontext. Voor de aquathermie wordt een ondergronds circuit opgezet dat water haalt uit de nabijgelegen Binnennete aan de Mosdijk en deze transporteert naar de aquathermie warmtepomp in de technische kelder van het Heilige Geesthuis. Om het Binnennete-circuit te kunnen realiseren zal een aanzuig- en lozingsleiding in één gestuurde onderboring worden voorzien tussen het perceel van de Heilig Geestsite en de Binnennete via het perceel Kerkstraat 3-5. Ter hoogte van de Binnennete aan de zijde van het perceel Kerkstraat 3-5 worden compacte RVS-warmtewisselaars op een nieuwe staalstructuur voorzien. De geothermische installatie (BEO-veld) wordt gerealiseerd door middel van verticale boringen ter hoogte van het binnenplein.

description: Het Godshuis Heilig Geesthuis bestaat uit vier gebouwen geschikt rond een binnenplaats. In het dossier worden de gebouwen als volgt benoemd; voorbouw gebouw A, westvleugel gebouw B, achterbouw gebouw C en oostvleugel gebouw D. Na een doorgedreven restauratie zal het gebouwensemble worden herbestemd als ‘Huis van het Kind’. De gebouwen worden aangepast aan de technische en comfort eisen van het Huis van het Kind met aandacht voor energie, duurzaamheid, toegankelijkheid , kindveiligheid en brand. De gebouwschil van gebouw A en C worden grondig gerenoveerd (herstel gevelparament, vernieuwen of restaureren buitenschijnwerk en vernieuwen van de dakbedekking). De houten draagstructuren, zowel verdiepingsvloeren als dakkap, worden in beide gebouwen doorgedreven hersteld of vernieuwd. Ook de nieuwbouw B wordt voorzien van een nieuwe ondergrondse kelder. De binnenplaats, die wordt vergroot door de afbraak van gebouw D, wordt volledig heraangelegd. Het project beoogt een duurzame verwarming van het Heilige Geestgebouw via een combinatie van aquathermie (warmte uit oppervlaktewater) en geothermie (BEO-veld). De toepassing van aquathermie kadert binnen een Europees Interreg-subsidieproject, waarbij het Heilige Geestgebouw fungeert als pilootproject voor duurzame energie in erfgoedcontext. Voor de aquathermie wordt een ondergronds circuit opgezet dat water haalt uit de nabijgelegen Binnennete aan de Mosdijk en deze transporteert naar de aquathermie warmtepomp in de technische kelder van het Heilige Geesthuis. Om het Binnennete-circuit te kunnen realiseren zal een aanzuig- en lozingsleiding in één gestuurde onderboring worden voorzien tussen het perceel van de Heilig Geestsite en de Binnennete via het perceel Kerkstraat 3-5. Ter hoogte van de Binnennete aan de zijde van het perceel Kerkstraat 3-5 worden compacte RVS-warmtewisselaars op een nieuwe staalstructuur voorzien. De geothermische installatie (BEO-veld) wordt gerealiseerd door middel van verticale boringen ter hoogte van het binnenplein.
